name: Dot Grid
description: WebGL2 canvas grid of dots that fills its container. Dots swell, stretch, glow and spring back as the cursor moves, and clicks send ripple shockwaves across the grid.
contents: Wrapper div sized to its parent with an absolutely positioned WebGL canvas
Instanced grid of dots rendered by GLSL shaders, circle or rounded square
behavior: Dots are pushed by pointer movement and spring back with spring-damper physics and neighbor coupling
Moving dots swell, stretch along their motion direction and blend from base to active color with a halo glow
Clicking inside the canvas emits a shockwave ring (up to 6 at once)
Intro animation pops dots in outward from the center with overshoot
Render loop sleeps once the grid settles and pauses when offscreen, tab hidden or paused
Respects prefers-reduced-motion by disabling swell, stretch, shockwaves and intro
Optional edge fade toward the borders
editableByProps: Dot size, spacing, shape, base and active colors, opacity, edge fade
Pointer reach and strength, spring bounce, tension and return time
Shockwave radius and strength, click shock on or off
Swell, stretch and glow amounts, intro on or off, pause, pixel ratio
Container sizing through className and style

fixed: Requires WebGL2; renders nothing if unavailable or shader linking fails
Parent must provide a height; the component fills 100% width and height
Canvas has pointer-events none, pointer and click tracking use window listeners, so interaction works over content layered above it
Color props accept only hex (3 or 6 digits), invalid values fall back to white
Maximum 6 simultaneous shockwaves, intro and shockwaves disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
Intro is read only at mount; changing the intro prop later has no effect
Touch devices get no hover effect, only pointer events and tap shocks
Large areas with small dots create many instances and run a CPU physics loop, costly on low-end mobile
